gaps.sentence: If only I ___ faster — we might still catch the train.
gaps.hint: if only plus could, present inability
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus 'could' expresses a present inability you regret: could run.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: Unless it ___ below five degrees tonight, the event will go ahead.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple even when referring to tonight: drops.

gaps.sentence: We will lose the deposit if we ___ the booking now.
gaps.explanation: The result clause carries 'will'; the if-clause stays in the present simple: cancel.

gaps.sentence: If the pain ___, stop taking the tablets and call your doctor.
gaps.hint: medical instruction with present after if
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: gets worse.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: Unless the strike ___, flights will be grounded all weekend.
gaps.hint: unless plus a present passive verb
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses use the present simple, here in the passive: is called off.
